question: How many independent, identical, successfully prepared trials give at least a 95% chance of emitting a direct 136.47 keV photon within 20 ns of preparation and eventually registering it in the LORAX full-energy peak in its cobalt-57 calibration geometry and matched live acquisition?

facts.preparation: One ordinary electronically occupied iron-57 nucleus prepared at time zero in the 136.47 keV (5/2-) level, with no later driving or feeding. The detector comparison treats the emission ensemble as orientation-averaged, with the calibration source placement and attenuation.
facts.event: Source emission of the direct nuclear 136.47 keV photon to the ground state within 20 ns, followed by eventual full-energy-peak registration of that photon in matched live acquisition.

measuredPopulationHalfLife.location: Bergmann, Javora and Smolyanskiy (2025), §4 Eq. (6), 136.5-keV level.

evaluatedPhotonWeights.location: Comments Table 5, Adopted column; scale has gamma(2,1) fixed at 100.

evaluatedTotalInternalConversionCoeffici.location: Evaluated table §2.2, gamma(2,1)(Fe) and gamma(2,0)(Fe) rows, alpha_T column.

detector.name: LORAX
detector.geometry: Collins et al. (2015) LORAX geometry: 1 g aqueous standard in a 2 mL ISO ampoule at 16.5 cm perpendicular distance from the detector window, with water-normalized attenuation.

publishedCalibration.location: Collins et al. (2015), §2.3.1 Eq. (1) and Table 3, 136.47 keV row
